notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch) was sufficient - site is a Next.js storefront that server-renders full page data (including the complete global mega-menu JSON) inline in HTML, no JS rendering needed. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only standard search/checkout/cart/admin/api paths blocked), so no policy_opt_out. Checked: (1) full sitemap.xml (6,545 URLs) - top-level /en/category/ nodes are only accessories, bathroom, bedroom, dining, lighting, living-room, with subcategories for accessories being carpets-rugs, cushions, decorative-accessories (candles-candleholders, figurines-sculptures, games, vases, wall-clocks), faux-trees-plants, fragrances, galleries-wall-art, mirrors, plaids - none seasonal/holiday-named. (2) Grepped sitemap for christmas/xmas/halloween/diwali/easter/valentine/thanksgiving/new-year/eid/ramadan/festive/festival/seasonal/holiday - only individual PRODUCT PDPs matched (e.g. christmas-tree-music-box, velvet-merry-christmas-garland, christmas-greenhouse-with-led, deco-object-easter-island, outdoor-sofa-set-holiday, plate/mug-flamingo-holidays) plus blog articles (Ramadan/Eid/Valentine's Day styling tips) - no category-level PLP URLs. (3) Extracted the full site-wide mega-menu JSON ("Menu: Mega Menu", "Kare Menu: Mega Menu") embedded identically in the RSC payload on 3 different pages (homepage, home-dcor-trends, decorative-accessories) - confirmed this is the exhaustive global navigation: Sofas/Armchairs/Living, Bedroom/Beds/Wardrobes/Nightstands/Dressers/Mattress, Dining/Dining Tables/Dining Chairs/Consoles/Sideboards, Lighting (Ceiling/Floor/Table Lamps), Accessories (Cushions/Pillows/Plaids/Bed Linen/Table Linen/Dinnerware/Fragrances/Mirrors/Decorative Accessories), plus Sale, B2B/Projects. Zero holiday/seasonal entries anywhere in this menu. (4) Checked editorial/ (design collections: Eclipse, Groove, Havana, Hebe, Omega, Pisa, Tango, Toulouse Travertine, Travertino - all product-design names, not seasonal) and promotion/ (sale, coming-soon-collection, new-collection-2026, online-exclusives - generic promos, not holiday-specific). (5) Found an "eid_gift" / "eid_gift_terms" i18n string on the homepage but it is a promotional banner ("For every spend of AED 1,000" gift-with-purchase, T&Cs apply) tied to a storewide spend threshold, not a product category or PLP - excluded per marketing/landing-page rule. (6) Directly probed guessed URLs for /en/christmas, /en/eid, /en/ramadan, /en/diwali, /en/halloween, /en/easter, /en/valentines-day, /en/new-year, /en/thanksgiving and their /en/category/ equivalents - all return HTTP 200 but are soft-404s (Next.js NOT_FOUND/notFound markers in payload), confirming none of these pages genuinely exist. (7) Checked for an Arabic-language storefront (site is UAE-based) - /ar redirects (301) back to the same English-locale content; no separate Arabic navigation/taxonomy exists to check. Conclusion: this is a furniture/home-decor retailer whose taxonomy is organized purely by room and product type; individual seasonal-themed decor items (Christmas ornaments/garlands, Easter Island decor objects, holiday-print tableware) exist as scattered PDPs inside generic categories (decorative-accessories, dinnerware) but the site itself never groups them into a dedicated seasonal/holiday category or PLP. No genuine seasonal category qualifies under the task's boundary rules.
